data.title: Clarithromycin
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Other antibacterials_

**Class:** Semisynthetic 14-membered macrolide

## Mechanism of action
- 50S ribosomal inhibitor; bactericidal against M. leprae; active against many atypical mycobacteria

## Pharmacokinetics
- Acid-stable; active 14-hydroxy metabolite; potent CYP3A4 inhibitor

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Atypical mycobacterial infections (backbone drug): M. marinum, M. chelonae/abscessus/fortuitum, MAC, M. ulcerans (with rifampicin)
- Leprosy (second-line, rifampicin-resistant regimens)
- Skin infections in penicillin allergy, acne (alternative), H. pylori (associated urticaria)
- Bacillary angiomatosis

## Dose & formulations
- 250–500 mg twice daily (NTM: 500 mg twice daily for months)

## Adverse effects
- Taste disturbance (metallic), GI upset
- QT prolongation, hepatotoxicity
- Possible increase in long-term cardiac mortality in heart disease patients (FDA advisory)

## Contraindications
- With colchicine in renal/hepatic impairment (fatal toxicity), simvastatin/lovastatin, ergot, pimozide; long QT

## Drug interactions
- Strong CYP3A4 inhibitor: colchicine, statins, cyclosporine, tacrolimus, carbamazepine, warfarin, rifampicin (reduces clarithromycin; rifabutin uveitis)

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid unless necessary (animal teratogenicity; old FDA category C).

## Viva points
- Key drug for NTM skin infections
- Colchicine + clarithromycin = fatal toxicity

_Sources: Khopkar ch.1 and ch.6; Wolverton 4e ch.9. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
